environment: KVM, QEMU 11.1.2 with optional bulk OUT pipeline; physical USB port 2-2; 800x480 RGB888. All module and raw USB operations inside the guest.
method: Snapshot controller registers with the normal driver active, unload it inside the guest, then claim both USB interfaces through usbfs.
Before each trial, issue application reset, restore captured mode and control registers, clear watermark, apply the selected configuration, wait 50 ms, then clear line-buffer status.
Submit one synchronous 128 or 129 KiB bulk OUT burst and sample status before sending the terminating zero-length packet. Repeat every configuration three times.
Restore original accumulation, PPE and ready settings; write zero to the high/low registers without verified readback; reload normal modules and run KMS checks.

restored.note: Initial accumulation register was 28009f41. Bit 15 is read-only ACLK-counter-max-hit status; writable bits match after restoration.

conclusions: All tested accumulation values were accepted in bits 31:16; both PPE values were accepted in bit 11.
No tested configuration moved the observed overflow boundary between 128 and 129 KiB.
This does not establish undocumented register dependencies, PPE polarity/function, high/low implementation, physical FIFO capacity, or whether overflow means pixel loss.

accumulation_2400_comparison.method: Alternate accumulation 0x2800 and 0x2400 for each burst size; three repetitions, application reset and mode restore before each burst. Sample status, last-frame peak and first-ITP level before terminating ZLP. No writes to high/low registers.
accumulation_2400_comparison.result: Both settings have identical peak-versus-burst scaling through 128 KiB, with overflow at 129 KiB in all three repetitions. No observed reduction in the burst-size boundary. First-ITP values varied and exceeded the programmed accumulation field.

register_semantics.high_low_registers: The manual describes water levels without specifying programmable thresholds. They may be indicators; RW access alone does not establish control semantics.
register_semantics.readback_evidence: Reads of 0x8034 and 0x8038 repeated the preceding valid register read on the tested adapter. Neither measurement values nor successful writes are established.
register_semantics.verified_peak_indicator: 0x8060[23:8], documented as last frame highest line buffer waterlevel; this was used for peak observations.
register_semantics.scope: Unchanged overflow after writes to 0x8034/0x8038 does not establish whether those registers are indicators, controls, inaccessible or unimplemented.
